module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 550

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/550](https://www.erdosproblems.com/550)
- [Ch77] Chvátal, V., Tree-complete graph Ramsey numbers. J. Graph Theory (1977), 93.
- [Li26] Li, E., *A Resolution of Erdős Problem 550 on Tree versus Complete Multipartite Ramsey
  Numbers*, [arXiv:2606.23659](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23659) (2026).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos550

/--
Let $m_1\leq\cdots\leq m_k$ and $n$ be sufficiently large. If $T$ is a tree on $n$ vertices
and $G$ is the complete multipartite graph with vertex class sizes $m_1,\ldots,m_k$ then prove that
$$R(T,G)\leq (\chi(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m_1,m_2})-1)+m_1.$$

This problem is #16 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

Li [Li26] proved this, combining an off-Turán tree-embedding theorem with a compactness theorem
for bounded-rank hypergraph obstructions. The linked formal proof states the bound for trees on an
arbitrary finite vertex type and with `K_{m_1,m_2}` written as a complete multipartite graph with
two parts; the statement below is the special case `V = Fin n`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos550/Main.lean#L80"]
theorem erdos_550 :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (m : Fin k → ℕ) (hm : Monotone m)
      (hm_pos : ∀ i, 0 < m i),
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
        ∀ (T : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), T.IsTree →
          SimpleGraph.graphRamsey T
            (SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph (fun i ↦ Fin (m i))) ≤
            (k - 1) * (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey T
              (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin (m ⟨0, by omega⟩)) (Fin (m ⟨1, by omega⟩))) - 1) +
                m ⟨0, by omega⟩ := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos550

status_issues.recorded: research solved, an unconditional formal_proof using lean4 link, and the docstring assertion that Li proved the problem.
status_issues.source_status: Erdős Problems currently labels #550 OPEN (LEAN). Its proof-claims page lists Li's work as a full proof claim, rather than an accepted solution. This conflicts with the cited arXiv v2, which expressly claims an unconditional Lean-verified resolution; it is a discrepancy between source status records, not evidence that the inequality is wrong.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/550/proof-claims displays 'OPEN (LEAN)', records a 'full proof claimed by Eric Li', and warns that appearing there 'does not mean that anyone associated with this site has examined any part of the proof'. Conversely, https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23659 states that the full unconditional proof has been formally verified in Lean.
status_issues.suggested_change: Reconcile the status records. If following Erdős Problems' current accepted-status classification, use research open and describe Li's work as a proof claim. If independent verification of the linked Lean proof justifies retaining research solved, document that basis and seek an update to the source's status. Do not change the mathematical statement merely because of this discrepancy.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses k instead of χ(G), represents every n-vertex tree on Fin n, and uses completeBipartiteGraph where the linked formal proof uses a two-part completeMultipartiteGraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every part is nonempty by hm_pos, so the complete multipartite graph has chromatic number exactly k. Every finite n-element vertex type is equivalent to Fin n; transporting a graph along that equivalence preserves treehood and both Ramsey numbers. The two bipartite representations are isomorphic via (0,x) ↦ Sum.inl x and (1,y) ↦ Sum.inr y. These identities and the finite-vertex-type equivalence were proved in the scratch file. Also, eventually atTop on ℕ is precisely existence of a threshold, uniform over the subsequently quantified trees. Thus these representation choices do not change the source's claim.

review.notes: The sole mathematical declaration matches Li's Theorem 1.1 and the original problem's inequality, including the threshold's dependence on fixed part sizes and its uniformity over trees. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully: checks cover graph relabelling, chromatic number, the two bipartite representations, k=2, n=0 and n=1, and small adjacency matrices. The finite Ramsey witness set is nonempty, so graphRamsey's sInf default is not reached here. The linked proof's statement and definitions were checked, and its source directory was scanned without finding sorry or custom axioms; the external project was not rebuilt. Chvátal's original publisher page was inaccessible, but its supporting result was read in the problem sources and Li's introduction; it is not separately asserted in this file.
